deities: Lord Ganesha (large ~8-ft self-manifested idol per local legend)

history.summary: Popular Ganesha temple on a hillock in the Ratanada area of Jodhpur, near Umaid Bhawan Palace. Local tradition says the temple has existed since 1459 (the Rao Jodha founding era) and that the ~8-ft tall, 5-ft wide Ganesha idol appeared naturally, rising out of the ground; it is still accessed through a grilled enclosure. It is a major Wednesday devotional spot and draws crowds for weddings and auspicious events (the first wedding invitation is traditionally sent here). FLAG: the 1459 date and the self-manifested idol claim come from local legend and travel listings, not archaeological sources (verify). CSV town 'Jodhpur' and spelling 'Ratnada' are fine - the locality is officially Ratanada; documented as such.

name: Ganesh Temple, Ratnada Hill
town_description: Jodhpur, the 'Blue City' and 'Sun City' of Rajasthan, is the historic capital of Marwar founded by Rao Jodha in 1459. Dominated by the massive Mehrangarh Fort, it is Rajasthan's second-largest city and a major tourist hub for Rajput heritage, blue-painted old-town houses, textiles, and handicrafts.

travel.railway: Short auto/taxi ride from Jodhpur Junction (Ratanada area, near Sojati Gate)
travel.road: Ratanada hill, near Umaid Bhawan Palace; drive up the hillock from the Ratanada area

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Wednesdays and Ganesh Chaturthi for the full devotional atmosphere
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer: morning aarti 5:30 AM to 6:00 AM, evening aarti 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM; Winter: 6:00 AM to 6:30 AM and 7:00 PM to 7:30 PM
